oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: P0 - serving-runtime high latency + container restarts in us-west-2. Auto-runbook triggered. Links: https://internal.incidents/23345 :rotating_light:
oncall-bot: Symptoms: high tail latency (>5s), continuous-batcher queue depth growing, several containers restarted by k8s on gpu-pool-7; potential OOM / CUDA failures in logs.
oncall-bot: Incident severity escalated to P0. Please ACK and join #eng-oncall.

alex.k: acked. jumping in. grabbing logs from the nodes.

maya.s: ack. I see repeated GPU driver disconnects in kube events: "Device plugin: container runtime runc: error: failed to start containerd-shim" - attaching recent pod logs.

jia: I have a customer report: model embeddings endpoint saw 10x latency and a couple 500s. Customer impacted: 2 active tenants on dedicated pool. Marking customer-abc as impacted.

harry: looks like continuous-batcher process on node gpu-7-2 shows a stuck batcher thread and then the container restarted by kube. stack trace shows locked mutex in batch_allocator.cpp at line 482.

alex.k: posting tail of container log: ```
2026-03-14T09:12:03Z ERROR runtime: cuda: cuCtxDestroy: unknown error
2026-03-14T09:12:03Z WARN continuous-batcher: queue_depth=12456, inflight_batches=0
2026-03-14T09:12:04Z INFO kubelet: killing container continuous-batcher (OOMKilled)
```

maya.s: interesting: queue_depth huge but inflight_batches=0 suggests batching deadlock (growth without dispatch). Possibly a kernel regression or tokenization causing 1M token requests.

ops-rotation: running quick mitigation: temporarily scale down continuous-batcher replicas to 2, enable backpressure throttle (batcher.max_queue=5000), and set model fallback to small-quantized variant for the impacted route. Commands: ```kubectl scale deploy/continuous-batcher --replicas=2 -n inference-prod && kubectl set env deploy/continuous-batcher -n inference-prod BATCHER_MAX_QUEUE=5000```

jia: applying policy now. Also routing rule: traffic.percentages for embeddings-route -> small-quantized: 30% for canary.

alex.k: after scaling down we see immediate reduction in new OOMs but latency still high for queued requests. We need to drain backlog without overwhelming remaining workers. Starting a rolling drain via: ```curl -X POST https://controlplane/rebalance -d '{"service":"continuous-batcher","mode":"drain","target":2}'```

maya.s: I see one node repeatedly flapping GPU driver: "NVIDIA kernel module lost" across gpu-7-2 and gpu-7-4. Node-level kernel messages show nv_peer_mem errors. Suggest cordoning gpu-7-2 and -4 to prevent new pods scheduling. 

harry: cordon + evict in progress: ```kubectl cordon gpu-7-2 && kubectl drain gpu-7-2 --ignore-daemonsets --force``` - evictions succeeding. Will watch for new restarts.

oncall-bot: Note: automatic rollback suggestion applied: route failover to hosted inference fallback for affected customers (customer-abc).

jia: customer-abc support notified. Ticket CREATED-1923 with mitigation steps and ETA for restoration ~30-45m.

alex.k: digging into the batcher code: reproducer shows a race when token length > 65k combined with special unicode char sequence causing the batch builder to loop and never emit a batch boundary. Patch idea: add soft cap on batch token accumulation and emit partial batches if threshold reached. Creating hotfix branch.

maya.s: agree. While we push hotfix, let's keep throttles conservative and keep small-quantized fallback at 50% for customers on dedicated pools.

harry: rolling restart of continuous-batcher pods on remaining healthy nodes to clear kernel-state and NVidia driver contexts. Restarting one at a time.

ops-rotation: monitoring metrics: queue_depth trend drops from 12k -> 900 over 12 minutes, tail latency 95p from 6.2s -> 1.1s. OOMs stopped. Marking mitigations effective.

alex.k: pushed hotfix branch and CI green. Plan to deploy hotfix to canary with 5% traffic in 10m, then ramp if stable. Hotfix limits batch token accumulation and adds defensive assert.

jia: customer-abc updated: they confirm reduced errors on their end, latencies improving.

oncall-bot: Incident update: mitigations applied, customer impact limited to 2 tenants, rollback not required. Monitoring for 1h.

maya.s: postmortem notes: root cause = continuous-batcher unbounded token accumulation when confronted with malformed tokenization output + intermittent GPU driver instability leading to OOMKills. Contributing factors: no soft cap on batch size, lack of circuit-breaker to fallback early, and scheduling allowed packing too many batchers on nodes with flaky drivers.

harry: follow-ups: 1) deploy hotfix across clusters; 2) add BATCHER_MAX_TOKEN_CAP config (default 51200); 3) add node health filter to scheduler for GPU driver flaps; 4) improve runbook steps for cordon+drain; 5) update alerting to fire earlier when inflight_batches==0 and queue_depth growth > threshold.

ops-rotation: assigning follow-ups to eng-runtime backlog and creating ENG-3456 runbook update.

alex.k: closing handoff to SRE for monitoring and long term fixes. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
